justification: The replication substituted a Laplace (MAP + diagonal) approximation for the paper’s mean-field VI to obtain (mu, sigma), which can affect the sensitivity ranking but preserves the core reduced-HMC idea. Under this setup, Case I matched the paper exactly on the number of influential parameters for tau=0.9 (4/6) and showed agreement between VI-HMC and full HMC posterior means, reproducing C1 and C3. For Case II, however, the number of influential parameters at tau=0.9 was 54/141 rather than the paper’s ~79/141, so C2 was not reproduced. The acceptance-rate advantage at fixed step size (C4) was mixed: slightly higher for VI-HMC in Case I at the canonical step but not in Case II, so we mark it as partially reproduced. The specific step-size-at-80%-accept claims cited in the paper reference other problems (Burgers, cone) that were not replicated here, so we mark C5 as not tested. Finally, the ESS-per-gradient was better for VI-HMC on the reported Case II metric, reproducing C6. Overall, some core findings (subset sufficiency in Case I, posterior agreement, ESS/grad efficiency) were reproduced, while others (subset size in Case II; fixed-step acceptance universally higher; large step-size gains) were not reproduced or not tested, yielding a PARTIAL verdict.
one_line_summary: Case I core results and ESS/gradient gains reproduce, but Case II influential-set size and acceptance/step-size advantages do not fully carry over under the Laplace-based replication.
